text: My main symptom is Chronic cough and fever. I also have Weight loss, Night sweats, Generalized weakness, Poor appetite.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The combination of fever, night sweats, significant weight loss, and chronic cough over six months is highly suggestive of tuberculosis, especially given your recent release from prison. While your initial sputum stain was negative, this can happen with paucibacillary disease; have you experienced any hemoptysis (coughing up blood) or shortness of breath?

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Sarcoidosis

The clinical picture of chronic cough, fever, weight loss, and night sweats combined with diffuse infiltrates on imaging, but negative TB testing (sputum, Quantiferon Gold, T-TB antibodies) and normal calcium, strongly points to sarcoidosis. The recent normal ACE and Calcium results do not rule this out, as they can be normal in early or localized disease.
